name: update-content
description: Discover new GitHub Pages sites with getGitHubPages.py and keep the splash-page YAML files in sync: add new sites to the appropriate file and remove dead ones.
prompt:
You maintain the Jekyll splash page at mrhunsaker.github.io. The home page layout (_layouts/home.html) renders three lists from YAML data files in _data/: personal.yml (Personal Projects: personal coding projects and published writings/chapters/manuscripts), projects.yml (Professional Projects: software tools, apps, APIs, and documentation sites -- the default category), and resources.yml (Instructional Materials: guides, courses, protocols, and reference sites for other people). Each entry has title, url, and optional description.

Steps:
1. Run `python3 getGitHubPages.py` in the repository root and parse its output lines of the form `- repo_name: https://mrhunsaker.github.io/repo_name/`. These are all live GitHub Pages sites for the account.
2. Read _data/personal.yml, _data/projects.yml, and _data/resources.yml. Build the set of URLs already listed across all three files.
3. ADD: any live site not already listed (except mrhunsaker.github.io itself, which is this splash page) is new. For each new site, fetch its GitHub repo description from https://api.github.com/repos/mrhunsaker/<repo_name> (use curl; a GITHUB_TOKEN env var may be set) to write a concise one-line description; fall back to a short description derived from the repo name if the API fails. Classify it: put it in resources.yml if it is instructional material (guides, lessons, protocols, courses, reference sites), personal.yml if it is a personal coding project or a published writing/chapter/manuscript, otherwise projects.yml. Append an entry with title, url, and description. Use the root-relative url form `/repo_name/` for sites on this account. Quote the description if it contains a colon followed by a space, a `#`, leading/trailing whitespace, or other YAML-special characters.
4. REMOVE dead sites: for every entry in the three YAML files whose url points to https://mrhunsaker.github.io/<repo_name>/ (root-relative or absolute) and <repo_name> is NOT in the live list from step 1, delete the entire entry from that file. Never remove entries whose url is external (a different domain, such as TVIResources.github.io, daisy.github.io, or vscode.dev) because those are not covered by getGitHubPages.py.
5. Preserve the comment header and existing formatting of each YAML file. Keep entries in their existing order; append new entries at the end of the appropriate file.
6. Validate that all three files still parse as YAML (e.g. `python3 -c "import yaml; [yaml.safe_load(open(f'_data/{n}.yml')) for n in ['personal','projects','resources']]"`).
7. Report exactly what you did: entries added (repo name -> file), entries removed as dead (repo name -> file), and files left unchanged.
